questions.q: What are the main parts of miniserve and how does work get handed from one to the next, from the command line to a rendered page?
facts: main parses args::CliArgs (clap), converts it with MiniserveConfig::try_from_args (config.rs), and passes the config to run, which builds the actix-web server

configure_app wires the request side: listing::file_handler when the served path is a single file; otherwise file_op::upload_file and file_op::rm_file plus an actix-files Files service whose listing renderer is listing::directory_listing
WebDAV is a separate dav_server handler backed by webdav_fs::RestrictedFs, registered only with --enable-webdav
listing::directory_listing builds the entry list and hands it either to renderer::page (maud HTML) or to archive::ArchiveMethod::create_archive, whose output is streamed through pipe::Pipe
errors defines StartupError and RuntimeError (with their HTTP status codes) and the middleware that renders error pages through renderer::render_error

questions.q: Where is the code that decides whether a request for a folder gets an HTML listing, a bare listing, an archive download, or an error?
facts: listing::directory_listing is installed as the actix-files files_listing_renderer (with show_files_listing), so it runs only for directory requests that the Files service resolves
With -I/--disable-indexing it returns a plain-text 404 'File not found.' before anything else, which also blocks archive downloads
A ?download=tar|tar_gz|zip query creates an archive, or returns 403 'Archive creation is disabled.' when that format's flag is off
Otherwise renderer::page renders the HTML listing, and returns the minimal raw table instead when ?raw=true

questions.q: Where are error responses turned into the styled HTML error page, and which errors stay plain text?
facts: errors::error_page_middleware, installed on the whole App with from_fn in main.rs, inspects responses after the handler has run

RuntimeError::error_response produces text/plain bodies (adding WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="miniserve" for InvalidHttpCredentials); the middleware rewrites only 4xx/5xx responses whose Content-Type is text/plain
It skips requests whose path is exactly "/upload" so the upload XHR gets plain text; that comparison is a literal string and does not account for --route-prefix

map_error_page replaces the body with renderer::render_error, using the Referer as the back address; the 'Go back to file listing' link is shown only when there is no route prefix and indexing is not disabled, so a random route is not leaked

questions.q: Where is the server's configuration kept at runtime, what is in it, and how do request handlers get to it?
facts: All runtime settings live in one struct, config::MiniserveConfig, built once from CliArgs by MiniserveConfig::try_from_args

Some fields are derived rather than copied from flags: file_upload is whether -u/--upload-files was given, rm_enabled is whether -R/--rm-files was given, and route_prefix comes from --route-prefix or six random hex characters with --random-route
run clones it into every worker's App as web::Data<MiniserveConfig> app data; nothing mutates it after startup

Handlers read it with req.app_data::<web::Data<MiniserveConfig>>() (upload_file, rm_file, handle_auth, directory_listing, map_error_page) or take it as a web::Data<MiniserveConfig> extractor (the api handler)

questions.q: Where is a visitor's chosen color theme stored, and where does the server's default theme come from?
facts: The visitor's choice lives only in the browser: updateColorScheme saves it in localStorage under 'theme' and sets a data-theme attribute on <body>; a 'storage' listener keeps other tabs in sync, and the server never sees it
The server default comes from -c/--color-scheme and -d/--color-scheme-dark (ThemeSlug values in MiniserveConfig)

At startup run concatenates the base stylesheet, default_color_scheme.css() and default_color_scheme_dark.css_dark() (wrapped in @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)) into one web::Data<String> that the css handler serves at css_route
The CSS is compiled at build time: build.rs compiles data/style.scss and every file in data/themes with sasso into OUT_DIR, and ThemeSlug::css embeds the results with include_str!

questions.q: What happens end to end when someone uploads a file from the web page?
facts: The page's JavaScript sends each file as its own multipart POST (XMLHttpRequest) to the upload form's action, {route_prefix}/upload?path=<current dir>, adding X-File-Hash and X-File-Hash-Function: SHA256 only when it managed to hash the file in the browser
file_op::upload_file sanitizes the path query parameter and returns 403 UploadForbiddenError unless it starts with one of the allowed upload directories (an empty list means anywhere)
Each file field goes through handle_multipart, which sanitizes its file name, to save_file, which first applies --on-duplicate-files: error (DuplicateFileError), overwrite, or rename to name-N.ext

save_file streams the data into a NamedTempFile (in --temp-directory if set, else the OS temp dir) and only renames it onto the target after the optional hash check passes; a mismatch deletes the temp file and returns UploadHashMismatchError

questions.q: When an HTTP request arrives, what middleware and routes does it pass through before a handler answers?
facts: App-wide middleware: DefaultHeaders built from --header, error_page_middleware, the access Logger, and Compress only when -C/--compress-response

The healthcheck, API, favicon and CSS routes are registered directly on the App; everything else goes into web::scope(route_prefix), which gets HTTP Basic auth (auth::handle_auth) only when auth entries exist

Inside the scope, /upload and /rm are POST-only resources (registered only when enabled and the served path is a directory), actix-files Files is mounted at "" behind a GET/HEAD guard, and OPTIONS/PROPFIND fall through to the read-only WebDAV dav_handler when --enable-webdav
When the served path is a single file, the scope only has listing::file_handler at "" and "/", which always returns that file
The App's default_service is error_404, which returns RuntimeError::RouteNotFoundError

questions.q: If I change sanitize_path in file_utils, what else is affected?
facts: upload_file and rm_file run the path query parameter through it (with conf.show_hidden) and then prefix-match the result against the allowed directories
handle_multipart uses it on each uploaded file name and as the hidden-path check for mkdir paths
The api DirSize handler in main.rs calls it with traverse_hidden = true, so hidden directories are allowed there regardless of -H

At startup config::validate_allowed_paths uses it to normalize --upload-files and --rm-files directories into the strings that upload_file, rm_file and the renderer's upload_allowed/rm_allowed checks compare against; an illegal path aborts startup

questions.q: If I change how the route prefix (--route-prefix / --random-route) is represented, what else depends on it?
facts: config.rs builds it as '/' plus the trimmed prefix, '/' plus six random hex characters, or an empty string, and prefixes the internal __miniserve_internal routes with it except under --random-route, so the random route is not leaked
main.rs mounts the auth-wrapped file-serving scope at it
listing.rs uses it to decide is_root, to strip it from the request path for encoded_dir, and as the base of the breadcrumb links
renderer.rs builds the upload and rm form actions as {route_prefix}/upload and {route_prefix}/rm

questions.q: Which type represents the logged-in user, and where does it get used?
facts: auth::CurrentUser { name } holds the Basic-auth user name for the request
handle_auth inserts it into the request extensions before checking the password, then rejects the request if no credential matches
directory_listing reads it from req.extensions() and passes it to renderer::page
Its only use in the page is the wget footer, which adds --ask-password --user '<name>' to the download command

questions.q: Which type represents one file or folder row in the listing, and what does it carry?
facts: listing::Entry: name, entry_type (EntryType::Directory or File), link, size (Option<ByteSize>, files only), last_modification_date and symlink_info
symlink_info is filled only when the entry is a symlink and --show-symlink-info is on (the read_link target)
For files, link is replaced by --file-external-url plus the relative path when that option is set

Directory sizes are not in Entry: the page's JavaScript POSTs {"DirSize": path} to the API for each directory row (updateSizeCells runs every second and caches results per path), and the server answers '-' unless --directory-size is on

questions.q: How would I add a new command-line option, and what do I have to touch for handlers to see it?
facts: Add a field with an #[arg(...)] attribute to args::CliArgs; most options also set env = "MINISERVE_<NAME>", and options that only make sense with uploads use requires = "allowed_upload_dir"
Add a matching field to MiniserveConfig and set it in the Ok(Self { ... }) literal at the end of try_from_args; the literal lists every field, so the compiler forces this
Handlers and the renderer only see MiniserveConfig (renderer::page takes &MiniserveConfig), never CliArgs
Shell completions and the man page are generated from CliArgs::command() (--print-completions, --print-manpage), so they pick up the new option automatically

questions.q: How would I add a new archive format to the folder download buttons?
facts: Add a variant to archive::ArchiveMethod; its snake_case serde/strum name becomes the ?download= value, and extension, content_type, is_enabled and create_archive each need an arm
is_enabled takes one bool per format (tar, tar_gz, zip), so a new format also needs its own CLI flag and MiniserveConfig field and a new argument at its call sites in listing.rs and renderer.rs
The buttons come from iterating ArchiveMethod::iter(), but the toolbar is only shown when tar_enabled || tar_gz_enabled || zip_enabled, so that condition needs the new flag too

directory_listing writes the archive into a pipe::Pipe on a separate thread while already returning a 200 streaming response; archive errors are only logged, so a failure shows up as a truncated or empty body, not an error status

questions.q: When --auth is set, is every endpoint behind the password?
facts: Basic auth is applied by wrapping only the web::scope(route_prefix) with HttpAuthentication::basic(auth::handle_auth), inside a Condition that is on only when auth entries exist
The healthcheck, API, favicon and CSS routes are registered on the App outside that scope, so they answer without credentials; the tests assert this for healthcheck, favicon and CSS
That includes the POST API: with --directory-size on, DirSize computes directory sizes for unauthenticated clients

handle_auth accepts when any configured RequiredAuth matches the user name and password (plain compare, or sha256/sha512 of the supplied password); otherwise InvalidHttpCredentials becomes a 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="miniserve"

questions.q: How do upload and delete stop a client from writing or deleting outside the served folder or the allowed directories?
facts: sanitize_path keeps only normal path components, resolves '..' by popping (so it can never climb above the root), and returns None for dot-prefixed components unless hidden files are allowed (-H)

upload_file and rm_file then require the sanitized path to start with one of the allowed directories (an empty list from a bare -u or -R means anywhere), else 403 UploadForbiddenError / RmForbiddenError
The canonicalized target must exist, but it is required to stay under the served root only when --no-symlinks is set; otherwise a symlink inside the root can lead outside it
The renderer's own upload_allowed/rm_allowed string-prefix check only hides the forms and delete buttons; the server-side checks are the ones in file_op

questions.q: Where are hidden files and symlinks filtered out, and do archive downloads respect the same rules?
facts: Plain file serving: actix-files only serves hidden files when -H turns on use_hidden_files, and with --no-symlinks the Files path_filter rejects any request path that has a symlink component under the served root
Listing: directory_listing skips entries that dir.is_visible rejects unless show_hidden, and skips symlinks when no_symlinks
WebDAV: RestrictedFs returns NotFound for hidden or symlinked paths and filters them out of directory reads
Archives get only a skip_symlinks flag and no hidden-files flag; the zip walker adds every entry, so dotfiles end up in archives even without -H
The zip symlink skip checks std::fs::metadata, which follows links, so is_symlink() is never true there and symlinks are not skipped
